title: 耶鲁研究员：从克拉苏到马斯克，财富如何摧毁共和制
speaker: William D. Cohan

segments.en: This piece that you have coming out, you used two very different historical examples.
segments.zh: 你即将发表的这篇文章中，用了两个截然不同的历史例子。

segments.en: One is in Rome with the guy who bankrolled Julius Caesar.
segments.zh: 一个是罗马，资助尤利乌斯·凯撒的那个人。

segments.en: And the other is, at the turn of 20th century, when Teddy Roosevelt broke up JP Morgan's wealth.
segments.zh: 另一个是20世纪初，西奥多·罗斯福拆分JP摩根的财富。

segments.en: Yeah, Crassus was the wealthiest person in the end of the Roman Republic.
segments.zh: 是的，克拉苏是罗马共和国末期最富有的人。

segments.en: He bankrolled Caesar. What he basically was use his enormous wealth to, well, they preserved the forms of the Republic.
segments.zh: 他资助了凯撒。他基本上是利用巨额财富，嗯，他们保留了共和国的形式。

segments.en: So the Senate still existed, right? All of these rules were there.
segments.zh: 所以元老院仍然存在，对吧？所有规则都在。

segments.en: In practice, Crassus and his wealth and other sort of Roman oligarchs combined to bypass all those things and rule the Republic directly.
segments.zh: 实际上，克拉苏和他的财富以及其他罗马寡头联手绕过了这一切，直接统治了共和国。

segments.en: And that led quite directly to the fall of the Republic and what became the Roman Empire.
segments.zh: 这直接导致了共和国的灭亡，以及后来的罗马帝国。

segments.en: Crassus used to say that you're not really wealthy unless you can afford to pay for a private army.
segments.zh: 克拉苏曾说过，除非你能负担得起一支私人军队，否则你算不上真正的富有。

segments.en: That's what the definition of sort of real wealth.
segments.zh: 这就是真正财富的定义。

segments.en: And by that standard, you know, the United States is a lot of people was real wealth.
segments.zh: 按照这个标准，美国有很多人拥有真正的财富。

segments.en: Republics have dealt with this problem through all of history.
segments.zh: 共和制在历史上一直面临这个问题。

segments.en: And this is the center, maybe the most important way in which a Republic falls that because Republics are very good at generating private wealth.
segments.zh: 这是核心，也许是共和制衰亡的最重要方式——因为共和制非常擅长创造私人财富。

segments.en: And then people with private wealth say, well, you know, there are only so many yachts I can buy.
segments.zh: 然后拥有私人财富的人会说，嗯，我能买的游艇是有限的。

segments.en: There are only so many in the modern context private jets I can buy.
segments.zh: 在现代，我能买的私人飞机也是有限的。

segments.en: But power is something that I can buy that has no rivals, right?
segments.zh: 但权力是我可以买到的、没有竞争对手的东西，对吧？
